findings_accepted: all four. My claim that only a new schema lease or a grant_writer change could close the duplicate write is WITHDRAWN -- it was wrong, and the reviewer's serialization proposal is right.

serialization.revalidated: store.py:499-588. ControlStore.transact takes BEGIN IMMEDIATE, RE-READS the replay inside that lock, runs the action under a savepoint, and journals and commits together -- so a second identical call blocks and then returns the committed result WITHOUT entering the action.
serialization.adopted: the profile effect, the revocation and the line release now happen inside one transact action, after the owned evidence and the exclusion are re-proved under the lock
serialization.revocation: back at COMPLETION where it was, which is also why neither of the two restored test methods needs editing
serialization.reentry: same-connection reentry is contained before the action runs: a nested transact on one connection is not a second transaction and would release the outer act's savepoint
serialization.retry_safety: ProfileRefusal is not a ContractRefusal, so it takes transact's fault branch -- ROLLBACK TO act then ROLLBACK -- leaving the committed intent and no completion. Nothing inside the action raises a DURABLE refusal, which would be journalled as a refused row and would turn a transient filesystem fault into a permanent one.
serialization.tradeoff: the store's write lock is held across a bounded local restoration, which the review explicitly accepted

object_binding.was: a pathname comparison before and after each command; the reviewer's runner replaced the path after the last check and before reset executed, and the outside tree was written anyway
object_binding.now: the checkout is HELD as an O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW descriptor and every command's path is derived from that descriptor immediately before it runs, then proved to still be the same object. A rename cannot redirect a descriptor and a symlink cannot become one, so the commands follow the checkout this profile was nominated over rather than whatever its old name now points at.
object_binding.runner_contract_unchanged: it still receives argv and nothing else; the descriptor does not cross into the child. What crosses is a path derived from it at the last possible moment.
object_binding.exact_missing_capability_named: resolving an open directory descriptor to a path needs /proc/self/fd. A deployment without it is told exactly that, by refusal, rather than quietly getting the weaker pathname behaviour.
object_binding.control_changed_meaning: the between-the-writes case no longer asserts a refusal: the substitution redirects nothing, so the restore succeeds over the held object and the outside tree is proved untouched
